story.headline: What makes food ‘organic’? For many consumers, the answer isn’t always on the label
story.summary: What makes food ‘organic’? For many consumers, the answer isn’t always on the label
story.score_reason: Organic standards explained, weak local angle

carousel.cover_headline:
What Does 'Organic'
Actually Mean?
It Depends Who You Ask.

slides.label: THE RESEARCH
slides.headline: 33 consumers filmed their own food to explain organic
slides.insight: New Zealand study; videos revealed habits that surveys alone miss.

slides.label: WHAT THEY FOUND
slides.headline: Shoppers define organic by trust, not just the label
slides.insight: Taste, quality, environment and safety all shaped their choices.

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.headline: New Zealand's organic sector was worth **NZ$1.18 billion** in 2024
slides.insight: Around three-quarters of survey respondents still bought organic food or drink.

slides.label: SOIL FIRST
slides.headline: Organic farming is understood as supporting soils, ecosystems and people
slides.insight: Certification tracks this standard across the full supply chain.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Grow one thing at home — even bean sprouts in a jar
slides.insight: One study participant grew sprouts and balcony greens after asking the same question.

sources: Organics Aotearoa New Zealand, 2025 market report (reported by The Conversation, 2026)
New Zealand government-led consumer survey, 2020 (reported by The Conversation, 2026)
Researcher study, 33 Chinese consumers of organic food in New Zealand (reported by The Conversation, 2026)
carousel.caption:
What does 'organic' actually mean? It depends who you ask.

A New Zealand researcher asked 33 Chinese consumers to film their own food — and found that trust matters more than labels.
Organic agriculture is broadly understood as supporting soils, ecosystems and people, but shoppers arrive at that idea in very different ways.
Do you look for an organic label when you shop, or do you go by something else?

Sources: Organics Aotearoa New Zealand, 2025 market report; New Zealand government consumer survey, 2020; researcher study on 33 Chinese consumers in New Zealand — all reported by The Conversation, 2026
